Change one setting at a time. **Predict what will happen before moving the slider**, then find a feature in the graph that supports or challenges your prediction.

[Open the lab in a full browser tab](lab/index.html){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} · [Go to the practice](practice.ipynb)

```{=html}
<iframe id="smoothing-lab" src="lab/index.html" title="Interactive smoothing lab: window widths, kernels, alignment, and rolling statistics" style="width:100%;height:1500px;border:1px solid #dce4e8;border-radius:12px;" loading="lazy"></iframe>
<script>
window.addEventListener("message", function (event) {
  const frame = document.getElementById("smoothing-lab");
  if (event.source === frame.contentWindow && event.origin === window.location.origin &&
      event.data && event.data.type === "smoothing-lab-height" &&
      Number.isFinite(event.data.height)) {
    frame.style.height = Math.max(500, Math.min(5000, event.data.height)) + "px";
  }
});
</script>
```

The real observations come from the course's [Yatir Forest temperature data](shani_2022_january.csv) and [Reykjavík weather data](../archive/data/Reykjaviik1990.csv). Synthetic signals are labeled in the data menu. The lab runs in your browser and requires no account.
